investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~136–145 seconds across all three checks, the eval runner timed out before createAgent() could return an agent identity or VM state, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing a full contract validation failure. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Highest evidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. The scheduler message 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' and 'No preemption victims found' directly state this.

[High evidence] Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's node affinity/selector targets only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, and those nodes are at capacity. If the selector was recently broadened or narrowed, the effective schedulable node count may have changed.

[Medium evidence] Cluster under-provisioning for remote-agent workloads: the cluster has only 2 nodes capable of hosting kata peer-pod VMs, and concurrent eval runs or production workloads may have saturated those nodes simultaneously.

[Low evidence, no supporting source proof] A recent change to pod resource requests or node affinity rules in the remote-agent workload definition could have increased per-pod resource consumption or restricted eligible nodes further — no source artifact in the supplied evidence confirms this.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available (allocatable > allocated) on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a different scheduling or API-level failure.

If a subsequent eval run with identical configuration succeeded and produced all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), the failure would be transient rather than a persistent capacity or configuration problem.

If the pod's node affinity/selector was found to target zero nodes (i.e., no nodes carry the required label at all), the root cause would be a misconfigured or missing node label rather than resource exhaustion.

If the 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm were found to have zero allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm (i.e., the resource is not installed or the device plugin is not running), the cause would be a missing device plugin rather than slot exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed, the shared scheduling root cause hypothesis would be weakened and the failure would be localized to the create path specifically.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated counts on all eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct check result rather than a scheduling timeout.
Add an eval that verifies the kata peer-pod device plugin is running and healthy on all nodes labeled for remote-agent workloads, catching plugin crashes before they cause pod scheduling failures.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that confirms at least N nodes match the remote-agent pod's node selector and have non-zero kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, alerting when the schedulable node count drops below a safe threshold.

Consider adding a latency-banded warning eval for remote-agent pod scheduling time (e.g., warn if scheduling takes >30s) to detect capacity pressure before it reaches the full Unschedulable state and eval timeout.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place new pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never produced a schedulable pod, so no agent identity or state was returned, leaving all required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) absent and triggering a contract validation failure.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the 2 eligible nodes. When the eval runner called createAgent to provision a remote agent pod, the scheduler reported "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and preemption was not possible. The pod remained unscheduled for ~143–145 seconds across all three checks, exceeding the eval timeout, so no agent was ever created, no state was polled, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state received zero evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes — concurrent workloads or prior eval runs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new probe pods.

Secondary: Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift — the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, meaning the schedulable node pool is effectively limited to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size.
Tertiary: A prior eval run or production workload leaked a remote agent pod (failed cleanup via withCleanup) that is still holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot, reducing available capacity.
Lower confidence: Cluster autoscaler is not configured or is unable to add kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes in time for the eval timeout window.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~136–145 seconds across all three checks, the eval runner timed out before createAgent() could return an agent identity or VM state, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing a full contract validation failure. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — the scheduler message is explicit that both capacity and affinity constraints are simultaneously violated.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=143335, status=fail — the check ran for ~143 s before failing, consistent with a pod stuck in Pending until the eval timeout.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=147309, status=fail — the same scheduling failure reproduced independently for the state check.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=151980, status=fail — the same scheduling failure reproduced independently for the runtime check.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent — consistent with the runner never reaching the post-scheduling steps in createAgent() (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885).
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no partial evidence was written, confirming the failure occurred before any evidence-write path in the runner.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885 only after requireOrgId() succeeds; the pod scheduling failure prevents this call from completing.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: [Highest evidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. The scheduler message 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' and 'No preemption victims found' directly state this.

[High evidence] Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's node affinity/selector targets only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, and those nodes are at capacity. If the selector was recently broadened or narrowed, the effective schedulable node count may have changed.

[Medium evidence] Cluster under-provisioning for remote-agent workloads: the cluster has only 2 nodes capable of hosting kata peer-pod VMs, and concurrent eval runs or production workloads may have saturated those nodes simultaneously.

[Low evidence, no supporting source proof] A recent change to pod resource requests or node affinity rules in the remote-agent workload definition could have increased per-pod resource consumption or restricted eligible nodes further — no source artifact in the supplied evidence confirms this.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available (allocatable > allocated) on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a different scheduling or API-level failure.

If a subsequent eval run with identical configuration succeeded and produced all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), the failure would be transient rather than a persistent capacity or configuration problem.

If the pod's node affinity/selector was found to target zero nodes (i.e., no nodes carry the required label at all), the root cause would be a misconfigured or missing node label rather than resource exhaustion.

If the 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm were found to have zero allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm (i.e., the resource is not installed or the device plugin is not running), the cause would be a missing device plugin rather than slot exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed, the shared scheduling root cause hypothesis would be weakened and the failure would be localized to the create path specifically.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated counts on all eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct check result rather than a scheduling timeout.
Add an eval that verifies the kata peer-pod device plugin is running and healthy on all nodes labeled for remote-agent workloads, catching plugin crashes before they cause pod scheduling failures.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that confirms at least N nodes match the remote-agent pod's node selector and have non-zero kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, alerting when the schedulable node count drops below a safe threshold.

Consider adding a latency-banded warning eval for remote-agent pod scheduling time (e.g., warn if scheduling takes >30s) to detect capacity pressure before it reaches the full Unschedulable state and eval timeout.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place new pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never produced a schedulable pod, so no agent identity or state was returned, leaving all required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) absent and triggering a contract validation failure.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the 2 eligible nodes. When the eval runner called createAgent to provision a remote agent pod, the scheduler reported "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and preemption was not possible. The pod remained unscheduled for ~143–145 seconds across all three checks, exceeding the eval timeout, so no agent was ever created, no state was polled, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state received zero evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' and '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' with no preemption victims available.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: remote-agent-state contract requires orgId, agentId, readyState, state — none reachable if the agent pod never schedules.
possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes — concurrent workloads or prior eval runs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new probe pods.

Secondary: Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift — the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, meaning the schedulable node pool is effectively limited to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size.
Tertiary: A prior eval run or production workload leaked a remote agent pod (failed cleanup via withCleanup) that is still holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot, reducing available capacity.
Lower confidence: Cluster autoscaler is not configured or is unable to add kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes in time for the eval timeout window.

If a passing sibling check or a different feature's eval successfully created a remote pod during the same run window, it would indicate the failure is not cluster-wide but scoped to a specific pod configuration or namespace quota.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that asserts kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is above a minimum threshold on eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, to catch exhaustion before the full probe times out.

Add an eval that verifies the count of schedulable nodes (nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector AND carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm) is at least N, alerting when the pool shrinks below a safe minimum.
Add a leaked-pod detection eval that lists all remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL and fails if any are found, catching withCleanup failures before they exhaust VM capacity.
Introduce a post-run cleanup verification step in the remote-agent eval suite that confirms no kata.peerpods.io/vm-consuming pods remain after each probe run.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-26T23:37–23:42Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required peer-pod VM onto any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was produced, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature had exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that support peer-pod VMs at the time of the eval run. The remaining 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request timed out unscheduled (~136–151 s), preventing agent creation and making it impossible for the eval to collect any required evidence. This is a cluster-infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; impact is scoped to the AURA observability eval suite.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after acquiring orgId; if the pod never schedules, createAgent cannot return and no evidence fields are populated.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:262-270: contract requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, message and asserts message containsIgnoreCase 'hello from aura' — none of these can be satisfied without a running agent VM.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes: concurrent eval runs, other workloads, or leaked/stuck peer-pod VMs from prior runs consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new agent pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not carry the label or taint required by remote-agent pods, meaning effective schedulable capacity is structurally limited to only 2 nodes regardless of load.

Tertiary — resource leak from a prior eval run that did not clean up its peer-pod VM: the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916) is responsible for teardown; if a previous run's cleanup failed, the VM slot would remain occupied.

Lower confidence — transient spike in concurrent remote-agent workloads from non-eval traffic consuming all VM slots at the moment the eval ran; no traffic signals are present in the evidence to confirm or deny this.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes peer-pod VM scheduling layer
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2/6 nodes is the direct cause of all three check failures. This is the infrastructure layer that provisions the VM backing each remote agent.
affectedAreas.details: 0/6 nodes schedulable: 2 with exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm quota, 4 excluded by node affinity/selector.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents eval feature — all three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (lines 183–185) failed with the same underlying scheduler error, indicating the entire feature's eval coverage is blocked by the capacity issue.
affectedAreas.details: remote-agent-create (required=true), remote-agent-state (required=true), remote-agent-runtime (required=false) all returned fail status.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — createAgent call for remote agent type
affectedAreas.reason: The runner branch at line 1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote'; this call depends on a schedulable peer-pod VM and cannot succeed when cluster capacity is exhausted.
affectedAreas.details: Source context lines 1913–1918 show the runner proceeds directly to createAgent after token and orgId checks.

affectedAreas.label: Expected-output contract — remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: The contract at lines 266–270 requires 5 evidence fields and a message assertion; all are unmet because the agent was never created.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes immediately for kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion using kubectl describe node; if slots are fully consumed, identify and terminate any stuck or leaked remote-agent pods from prior eval runs.
Audit the withCleanup wrapper in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to confirm it reliably releases kata.peerpods.io/vm resources after each eval run, including on error and timeout paths.

Determine whether the 4 nodes excluded by node affinity/selector are intentionally ineligible for peer-pod VMs or whether a configuration drift has reduced the effective schedulable node pool below the minimum needed for concurrent eval runs.

Consider adding a pre-flight check in the remote-agent eval runner that queries available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity before attempting agent creation, and returns a descriptive SKIP or WARN status instead of timing out after 136–151 s.

Evaluate whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on the 2 eligible nodes is sufficient for the expected concurrency of eval runs plus any production workloads sharing the same resource; scale capacity or add eligible nodes if not.

Once the scheduling issue is resolved, re-run all three remote-agents checks to confirm they return to a passing state and that all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are populated.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval probe in isolation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the scheduling failure is persistent or has self-resolved; a pass would indicate transient capacity exhaustion.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on peer-pod-capable nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms whether VM slots are exhausted and how many are allocated vs. available on the 2 schedulable nodes.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List all pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resource requests across all namespaces
recommendedVerifierProbes.command: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].resources.requests["kata.peerpods.io/vm"] != null) | {name: .metadata.name, namespace: .metadata.namespace, phase: .status.phase}'
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether leaked or stuck eval pods are consuming VM slots, supporting or refuting the resource-leak hypothesis.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check node labels and taints on all 6 cluster nodes to verify affinity/selector coverage
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the 4 nodes excluded by affinity/selector are structurally ineligible (by design) or have experienced a label/taint drift that reduced schedulable capacity.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together to confirm shared failure scope
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Validates that all three checks share the same infrastructure dependency and that resolving the scheduling issue restores all of them simultaneously.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes shows available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., a policy or quota change) would need to be investigated.

If the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime checks all pass on an immediate re-run without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than a persistent exhaustion condition.

If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass, the root cause would be localized to the runtime check's specific pod configuration rather than shared cluster capacity.

If the 4 nodes excluded by affinity/selector are found to have been recently relabeled or tainted, the structural capacity limit hypothesis would shift toward a node configuration change as the primary cause.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource requests are found on the cluster from non-eval workloads, the exhaustion would be attributable to leaked eval pods rather than competing production traffic.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-scheduling capacity eval that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested across all nodes and fails with a warning if available slots fall below a configured minimum threshold, catching exhaustion before agent creation is attempted.
Add a resource-leak detection eval that lists all remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL (e.g., 10 minutes) and flags any that were not cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies at least N nodes carry the labels/selectors required by remote-agent pods, alerting if the eligible node count drops below the minimum needed for scheduling.

Introduce a historical pass/fail trend eval for remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime so that correlated multi-check failures trigger an escalation path distinct from single-check flakes.
